newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Victoria state buys equipment for fibre centre.
newsitem.headline: Victoria state buys equipment for fibre centre.

text.p: The state of Victoria has tendered successfully to buy research and development equipment in Britain for a proposed A$30 million Australian Fibres and Textiles Education Centre (AFTEC), Premier Jeff Kennett said.

The equipment, to be bought for A$4.6 million, will be moved from the International Wool Secretariat's Ilkley facility and be installed at the AFTEC training centre in Geelong, Kennett told a wool conference on Thursday. Financial support from the federal government and the wool industry would be money better spent than on wool promotion, Kennett said.

Announcing the purchase at the Wool Council of Australia annual conference, Kennett castigated Australian industries for being "a long way behind" counterparts elsewhere in the world, or for being virtually non-existent.

He questioned why Australian wool was shipped offshore as a bulk commodity instead of being turned into leading-edge textiles in Australia. AFTEC was designed to help resolve this in the wool industry through training and education, he said.

The Victorian government is seeking funds from the federal government to help support AFTEC, which will require a total of A$14.0 million in capital investment and a further A$2.5 million in annual funding, Kennett said.
AFTEC will be applied to cotton and other fibres and textiles as well as wool.
"There's so much footloose industry in Japan and elsewhere but they don't even look to Australia," Kennett said in pressing his case for Australian tax reform.
